text:
Arjun Rao: Quick sync  We need a concrete escalation + handoff flow for regional residency violations when runtime falls back. Legal keeps asking for an operator path they can audit.

Hanna Li: Agree. Proposal: if fallback would break residency we attempt three steps: 1) local retry window (50ms), 2) cached-response/approximate read if allowed, 3) escalate to human review with escrow envelope.

Marta Ruiz: How do we define "approximate read"? For embeddings we can return cached embedding vector; for generation, maybe a summarized safe fallback. Need strict rules per API type.

Arjun Rao: Good point. Let's codify per-product policy: embeddings=cache-ok, text-generation=reject or escrow, rerank=cache-degraded. We'll map to tenant policy granularity.

Hanna Li: Implementation sketch: proxy checks tenant.residency + tenant.policy. If fallback_needed and policy=="escrow": proxy constructs an escrow_envelope (AES-GCM + KMS-wrapped key), writes claim to escrow-store (immutable), tags telemetry, then forwards envelope to secondary with envelope-ref. Secondary must call control-plane KMS to unwrap on demand.

CI-bot: build: residency-escrow: test coverage 82% on staging; unit + integration hooks passing.

Marta Ruiz: Escrow-store must be append-only and signed. Legal requires immutable chain-of-custody. Could use object storage with WORM + signed manifests.

Arjun Rao: Runbook step: when escrow-forward happens, runbook should alert oncall and create an incident-lite with tenant id + envelope-ref + reason. Oncall then confirms with security/legal and approves key unwrap if required.

Hanna Li: We should avoid manual unwrap for scale. Prefer automated unwrap when tenant has "fallback_approval": true in enterprise settings. Otherwise manual flow. Also add TTL for ephemeral keys (e.g., 7 days) and auto-rotate.

Marta Ruiz: Metric ideas: fallback_attempts, fallback_accepted, fallback_rejected, escrow_created, escrow_unwraps, avg_escrow_encrypt_ms, p95_kms_latency. Tag by tenant.region and SLA_tier.

Arjun Rao: Storage retention: legal asks 7 years immutability for chain-of-custody logs, but payloads in escrow we should auto-delete after 90 days by default unless explicitly archived by legal hold. Need cost estimate.

Legal-Bot: Note from legal: retention for audit logs (events) = 7 years. Retention for escrowed customer payloads = customer choice or court/legal hold. Default deletion policy OK with consent.

Hanna Li: Operator tooling: UI to list active escrows per-tenant, search by envelope-ref, and a "request-unlock" workflow that records approver, justification, and time. Events go to immutable audit log.

Marta Ruiz: Performance: encrypt+wrap adds ~3-6ms on GPU hosts, ~15-40ms on CPU nodes under load. We'll benchmark for p99 tail. If unacceptable, we can gate escrow behind SLA tier.

Arjun Rao: Security checklist: (1) ephemeral keys KMS-only, no plain-key stored, (2) escrow-store encrypted at rest, (3) RBAC for unwrap operations, (4) HSM-backed KMS for EU customers if required.

CI-bot: test-run: escrow-e2e smoke passed on staging cluster eu-1. Telemetry flags present.

Hanna Li: Action items: Arjun to draft API-level contract (headers + error codes), Marta to spec escrow-store and retention, Hanna to own runbook + operator UI mockups, Legal to confirm retention/legal-hold edgecases.

Marta Ruiz: I'll also run a cost impact estimate for 1k escrows/day over 3 years (object storage + KMS ops).

Arjun Rao: Thanks. I'll open the design PR with sequence diagrams and the minimal proxy changes. Will ping this thread when ready.

Legal-Bot: Reminder: include sample audit transcript format in PR (signed manifests + operator approval records).
